subject: physics
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: The charge stored on a 470 µF capacitor at 9.0 V is:
The field lines of a radial gravitational field around a point mass:
options: point radially inward toward the mass
questions.explain: Field lines point in the direction of the force on a test mass, which is radially inward toward the attracting mass.

questions.q: If the voltage across a capacitor is doubled, the energy stored:
questions.explain: Since E = ½CV², energy is proportional to V², so doubling V multiplies energy by 4.

questions.q: The electric potential energy of two point charges Q and q separated by r is:
questions.explain: E_p = Qq/(4πε₀r), positive for like charges and negative for unlike charges.

questions.q: At the surface of the Earth (radius R, mass M), g equals:
questions.explain: g = GM/R² evaluated at the Earth's surface.

questions.q: For a discharging capacitor, the current through the resistor:
options: decreases exponentially with the same time constant as the charge
questions.explain: I = I₀e^(−t/RC), decaying exponentially with the same time constant RC as the charge.

questions.q: The electric field between two parallel plates a distance d apart with potential difference V is:
questions.explain: For a uniform field between plates, E = V/d.

questions.q: Coulomb's law for the force between two point charges is:
questions.explain: F = Qq/(4πε₀r²), an inverse-square law analogous to gravitation.

questions.q: A 100 µF capacitor is charged to 12 V. The energy stored is:
Equipotential surfaces in a gravitational field are:
questions.explain: Equipotentials are always perpendicular to field lines, so no work is done moving along them.

questions.q: For a circular orbit, the centripetal acceleration equals:
options: the gravitational field strength at that radius
questions.explain: Gravity provides the centripetal force, so a = v²/r = GM/r² = g at that radius.

questions.q: The gradient of a gravitational potential against distance graph gives:
options: the field strength (with a sign change)
questions.explain: g = −dV/dr, so field strength is the negative gradient of the potential.

questions.q: Escape velocity from a planet's surface is given by:
questions.explain: Equating kinetic energy to the magnitude of potential energy gives v_esc = √(2GM/R).

questions.q: If the distance between two masses is doubled, the gravitational force between them becomes:
questions.explain: With an inverse-square law, doubling r reduces the force by a factor of 2² = 4.

questions.q: Newton's law of gravitation states that the force between two point masses is proportional to:
options: the sum of the masses and inversely proportional to r²
the product of the masses and inversely proportional to r²
the sum of the masses and inversely proportional to r
the product of the masses and inversely proportional to r
questions.explain: F = GMm/r², so the force is proportional to the product of the masses and follows an inverse-square law with separation.

questions.q: A key difference between gravitational and electric fields is that:
options: electric fields do not have potential
electric fields can be attractive or repulsive while gravity is only attractive
questions.explain: Charge has two signs giving attraction or repulsion, whereas mass gives only attractive gravity.

questions.q: The electric force between two like charges is:
questions.explain: Like charges repel; only unlike charges attract, unlike gravity which is always attractive.

questions.q: The unit V m⁻¹ for electric field strength is equivalent to:
questions.explain: V m⁻¹ = (J C⁻¹)/m = N C⁻¹, since J = N m.

questions.q: Capacitance is defined as:
questions.explain: Capacitance C = Q/V, the charge stored per unit potential difference.

questions.q: The time constant of an RC circuit is:
questions.explain: The time constant τ = RC, with units of seconds.

questions.q: When a capacitor discharges through a resistor, the charge follows:
questions.explain: Discharge is exponential decay: Q = Q₀e^(−t/RC).

questions.q: As you move from the Earth's surface to infinity, the gravitational potential:
questions.explain: V = −GM/r increases (becomes less negative) toward zero as r increases to infinity.

questions.q: The work done moving a mass along an equipotential surface is:
questions.explain: There is no change in potential along an equipotential, so no work is done.

questions.q: Gravitational forces between two masses are:
options: attractive or repulsive depending on sign
questions.explain: There is only one sign of mass, so gravitational forces are always attractive.

questions.q: The orbital speed of a satellite in a circular orbit of radius r is:
questions.explain: Setting GMm/r² = mv²/r gives v = √(GM/r).

questions.q: The gravitational potential energy of a mass m at potential V is:
questions.explain: Potential energy E = mV = −GMm/r for a mass m in the field.

questions.q: Gravitational potential at a point is defined as:
options: the work done per unit mass to bring a mass from infinity to that point
the work done to move a unit charge
the force per unit mass at that point
the energy stored per unit volume
questions.explain: Gravitational potential V is the work done per unit mass in bringing a small test mass from infinity to the point.

questions.q: Electric field strength E at a point is defined as:
questions.explain: E = F/Q, the force per unit positive test charge.

questions.q: The energy stored in a capacitor is given by:
questions.explain: Energy = ½QV = ½CV² = ½Q²/C, the area under a charge–voltage graph.

questions.q: Equipotentials around a point charge are:
questions.explain: Equipotentials around a point charge form concentric spheres, perpendicular to the radial field lines.
